'''''Ruscus hypoglossum''''' is  a small evergreen shrub with a native range from [[Italy]] north to [[Austria]] and [[Slovakia]] and east to [[Turkey]] and [[Crimea]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Halada | first=Ľ. | title=''Ruscus hypoglossum'' L. in Slovakia | url=https://www.upjs.sk/public/media/5524/thaiszia-4-183-195-1994-halada.pdf | journal=Thaiszia | volume=4 | pages=183–195 | issn=1210-0420}}</ref> Common names include '''spineless butcher's-broom''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''mouse thorn''' and '''horse tongue lily'''. The [[Binomial nomenclature|species name]] comes from two Greek words ὑπό (''hypo'') and γλῶσσα (''glōssa'') meaning ''under'' and ''tongue''.

==Description==
The mature plant shrub will eventually reach about {{convert|18|in|cm|abbr=on|order=flip}} in height. It has a creeping rootstock and leaf-like [[phylloclade]]s or flattened stems that are about {{convert|3|in|cm|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} long to {{convert|1+1/2|in|cm|0|abbr=on|order=flip}} wide tapering at both ends. True leaves are smaller green appendages around the flowers. Small yellow flowers bloom in the axil of a leaf-like bract {{convert|1|-|1.5|in|cm|1|abbr=on|order=flip}} long on upper side of phylloclade. Plants are [[dioecious]], with male and female flowers produced on separate plants.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Reproductive biology of ''Ruscus hypoglossum'' L. in Slovakia|first1=Ľubos|last1=Halada|first2=Oľga|last2=Erdelská|date=2005|journal=Acta Biologica Cracoviensia. Series Botanica|volume=47|issue=1|pages=213–217|url=https://abcbot.pl/pdf/47_1/27halada.pdf}}</ref> Fruit is a rarely produced red globose berry {{convert|0.25|to|0.5|in|cm|1|abbr=on|order=flip}} wide.<ref name=UCON>{{cite web|url=http://titanarum.uconn.edu/198500092.html |title=''Ruscus hypoglossum''|work=University of Connecticut - Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Plant Growth Facilities|accessdate= 19 March 2012}}</ref>

==Etymology==
''Ruscus'' is derived from an old [[Latin]] name for prickly plants.<ref name= "gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp 209, 336</ref>

The specific epithet ''hypoglossum'' is derived from [[Greek language|Greek]] and means 'sheathed beneath' or 'below-a-tongue'. The name is in reference to the [[cladode|cladodes]] of this species, which extend beneath the flowers.<ref name= "gledhill" />
